sheet-71-1.description: The right-hand strip of sheet 71 follows Ocean Avenue north from the United States Life Saving Station through Normandie by the Sea, at 120 feet to an inch with north up. The Shrewsbury River lies to the west and the Atlantic Ocean to the east. Ocean Avenue, 55 to 60 feet wide with four- and six-inch water pipes, runs on the river side of the double track of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, with the bulkhead along the ocean. The dominant feature is the Hotel Normandie, a long frame hotel with casino, bowling alley, kitchen, help's quarters and carriage house, a dock and a long pier into the river, and an underground oil tank and gas machine; a night watchman in summer and a caretaker in winter are noted. South of it is Mrs. Earl's large cottage with an elevated water tank and an automobile house on a lot reaching into the river, and a dilapidated building beyond. On the ocean side stand the Normandie railroad station and a bath house. At the north end are the cottage of Jos. Wheelock and another dwelling. House numbers 2651 to 2676 are printed along the avenue; key numbers 178 and 179 refer to the key map. The strip carries the scale bar and ends at the match lines to sheet 70 and to the left strip of this sheet.
notes: Hotel Normandie with casino, bowling alley, dock and pier.
The printed scale bar (50 ft divisions) does not match the 120 ft to an inch of the sheet heading; the fit uses 3.289 px/ft from sheet 70.

Placed from one point carried from part 2, which is placed on the J. C. Duncan cottage drawn also on Highland Beach 1907 sheet 72; the Hotel Normandie grounds then lie at today's Normandie Place. Low confidence.

Printed sheet 71 (N.J. Coast vol. 1), 120 ft to an inch (the printed 50 ft bar is wrong). Two strips along Ocean Av, north up: part 1 right strip (Normandie by the Sea, Hotel Normandie), part 2 left strip (Navesink Beach). Placed from the north: part 2 on the J. C. Duncan cottage drawn also on Highland Beach 1907 sheet 72-3 (fixed coordinates from that placement), part 1 carried from part 2; rotation from the modern road. This puts the Hotel Normandie grounds at today's Normandie Place. The chain from Sea Bright (sheet 70) would put it about 480 m further north; low confidence.

sheet-71-2.description: The left-hand strip of sheet 71 carries Ocean Avenue north through Navesink Beach towards sheet 72, at 120 feet to an inch with north up. The Shrewsbury River is to the west and the Atlantic Ocean to the east. Ocean Avenue, 55 feet wide with a six-inch water pipe, runs on the river side of the double track of the Central Railroad of New Jersey, with the bulkhead beyond. The river side is lined with summer cottages on lots running down to an irregular shore with filled projections: from the north, J. C. Duncan, J. T. Hetterick with an automobile house, Pette, Mrs. W. H. Broadwell, Tyson, Edwin Arden, the Tower House with a cottage and automobile house, the E. Thomas estate, McVicker, a second Tyson cottage, Mrs. Holmes, Mrs. Hecker, a plastered cottage and further dwellings at the south end. The small Navesink Beach railroad station stands on the ocean side of the avenue. The name Navesink Beach is lettered along the lots. House numbers 2801 to 2826 are printed along the avenue and key numbers 181 and 182 refer to the key map. The strip ends at the match lines to sheet 72 at the top and the right strip of this sheet at the bottom.
notes: Navesink Beach is today part of Sea Bright north of Normandie.
Placed on the J. C. Duncan cottage, drawn on this sheet and on Highland Beach 1907 sheet 72, through that sheet's placement (fixed coordinates). Low confidence.

sheet-9999997-1.description: The southern strip of sheet 70 follows Ocean Avenue through the northern part of Sea Bright, from the Sea Bright railroad station at its south end to the Sea Bright borough limit at its north end, a stretch of about 2,500 feet. The sheet is drawn at 120 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right. The Shrewsbury River lies along the top of the strip and the Atlantic Ocean along the bottom. Between them run the double track of the Central Railroad of New Jersey and Ocean Avenue, here on the ocean side of the railroad until a crossing just short of the borough limit, where the avenue swings over to the river side. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn along the avenue. The river side is divided into narrow lots carrying small frame cottages, stables and automobile houses, with a boat house near the north end; the station building and its long platform shed stand at the south end, with a tower hydrant beside it. The ocean side is taken up by large summer estates and cottages, each lot running from the avenue to the beach: Colonel E. C. P. Lewis's estate, Mrs. W. W. Shippen, Mrs. Manning, H. Wilson, the Achelis cottage Inbermara, General Louis Fitzgerald's estate, E. S. Auchincloss's estate, W. B. Wells, the Shippen estate, John R. Rutherford, Camp, Dr. Janeway, J. Wood, W. H. Hall's Monmouth, Hendricks and the Reiley estate. House numbers 2501 to 2529 and 2545 to 2570 are printed along the avenue. Key number 175 and 171 refer to the adjoining key map. The word Sea Bright is lettered across the strip.
notes: Ocean Avenue is today Ocean Avenue (NJ 36); south of the crossing its east line matches modern parcel lines, north of it the 1907 avenue lay west of the railroad.
The railroad (Central R.R. of N.J.) along the peninsula has since been abandoned.
Placed from eight modern parcel corners on the east line of Ocean Avenue matched to the drawn ocean-side lot lines; all along one line, so a helmert fit.

Printed sheet 70 (N.J. Coast vol. 1); canvas label 9999997. 120 ft to an inch, north to the right. Part 1 bottom strip: Ocean Av, Sea Bright, from Sea Bright R.R. station to the borough limit; part 2 top strip: Ocean Av from the borough limit to the U.S. Life Saving Station (withheld, see unplaced); part 3 inset: Robert Hartshorne estate, Highlands of Navesink (not placed). Part 1 placed from 8 modern parcel corners matched to the ocean-side lot lines (1-D match, 9 of 13 lines within 4 m). North of the borough limit old Ocean Av ran west of the railroad, about 40 m west of modern Ocean Avenue (NJ 36).
